title: ANEMIA, CONGENITAL, NONSPHEROCYTIC HEMOLYTIC, 4

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia-4 (CNSHA4), due to glucose phosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency, is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the GPI gene (172400) on chromosome 19q13.11.

paragraphs.text: Glucose phosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency is an autosomal recessive cause of hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia. It most often presents as chronic hemolysis that improves after splenectomy (Shalev et al., 1993). In a review, Arnold (1979) noted that patients had a typical nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia, with hemolytic crises during acute infections. Baughan et al. (1968) described hereditary hemolytic anemia with GPI deficiency as a new enzyme defect of human erythrocytes, and Paglia and Valentine (1974) reviewed hereditary GPI deficiency.

paragraphs.text: Hutton and Chilcote (1974) observed 8 children (5 living, 3 deceased) with severe hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia caused by GPI deficiency in 2 families from Kentucky and Indiana. All affected children were severely anemic in early life, and some depended on transfusion before splenectomy. Three deaths occurred in young patients who either did not receive adequate blood transfusions or whose parents refused to allow splenectomy. Growth and development were surprisingly normal, and no patient died of infection.
